st: Combine the chicken, [[0.5 cup]] soy sauce, [[0.5 cup]] vinegar, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a bowl.
Marinate for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Move the chicken and marinade to a pot, add [[0.5 cup]] water and bring to a boil without stirring.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, turning the chicken once, until it reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken and pat dry. Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and brown the chicken for 3 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, boil the sauce uncovered for 8 minutes until reduced and glossy. Add [[1 tsp]] sugar if you like.
Return the chicken to the sauce, coat well and serve with steamed rice.
Put the pork in a pot with [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Skim off the foam for the first few minutes.
Add the onion and tomatoes, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tamarind paste and [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce.
Add the radish and cook 8 minutes.
Add the green beans and peppers and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook 2 minutes until wilted.
Taste, add salt if needed, and serve hot with rice.

ing: pork belly or boneless pork shoulder with skin
st: Pat the pork dry. Pierce the skin all over with a skewer or fork.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce with the pepper and rub it into the meat side only.
Lay the pork skin-side up and rub [[3 tbsp]] salt on the skin. Chill uncovered overnight for dry, crisp skin.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Brush off the extra salt.
Arrange the lemongrass, garlic, onions and green onions on the meat side and roll or fold the pork tightly, tying with kitchen string.
Brush the skin with [[2 tbsp]] oil. Roast on a rack for 2 hours 30 minutes.
Raise the oven to 475°F (245°C) and roast 20 to 30 minutes until the skin blisters and crackles. Watch carefully so it does not burn.
Rest for 20 minutes. The center should reach at least 145°F (63°C).
Chop with a heavy knife and serve with liver sauce or vinegar dip.

ing: flour stick noodles or chow mein
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large wok over medium-high heat.
Cook the garlic and onion for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until pink.
Add the carrots and cabbage and cook 3 minutes.
Pour in [[1.5 cups]] broth, [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] oyster sauce and the pepper and bring to a simmer.
Add the noodles and toss, cooking 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are tender.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Mix the pork, carrot, onion, garlic, 1 egg, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce, salt and pepper until well combined.
Cook a small test spoonful in a pan and taste, then adjust the seasoning.
Lay a wrapper in a diamond shape and place [[2 tbsp]] filling near one corner.
Fold the corner over, tuck in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Seal the end with beaten egg.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and the pork inside reaches 160°F (71°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chili sauce.
Place the oxtail in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil, skimming foam.
Simmer covered for 2 hours 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil with annatto for 2 minutes, then discard the seeds and keep the colored oil.
Cook the onion and garlic in the colored oil for 4 minutes.
Stir the onion mixture into the pot with [[0.5 cup]] peanut butter.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] rice flour with some broth and stir in to thicken for 10 minutes.
Add eggplant and beans and cook 6 minutes, then add bok choy for 2 minutes.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and serve with rice and [[2 tbsp]] shrimp paste on the side.

ing: raw yolk cooked on the hot plate, optional
st: Boil the pork belly in salted water for 40 minutes until tender, and it reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Drain and pat dry, then grill or broil for 8 minutes per side until the skin is crisp.
Chop the pork into very small pieces.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Add the pork and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chili, [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[0.25 cup]] calamansi juice and pepper and stir.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] mayonnaise off the heat.
Make a small well, crack in the egg and let it cook on the hot pan, mixing in at the table.
Serve sizzling with extra lime.

ing: peeled, seeded and cut in wedges; or use chayote
st: Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the garlic, onion and ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Pour in [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce and cook 1 minute.
Add [[6 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add the papaya and simmer 10 minutes until tender.
Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part.
Stir in the spinach and pepper and cook 2 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls with steamed rice.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce, [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, pepper and 6 minced garlic cloves in a bowl.
Add the beef and marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and fry the 4 remaining minced garlic cloves until golden.
Add the rice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and stir-fry for 5 minutes. Keep warm.
Cook the beef with its marinade in a hot pan for 6 minutes until the liquid cooks off and the edges brown.
Wipe the pan, heat [[3 tbsp]] oil and fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the beef with garlic rice and a fried egg on each plate.
Chill four tall glasses in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Spoon a tablespoon of red beans, coconut and ube jam into each glass.
Add one slice of leche flan to each glass.
Fill each glass with shaved ice, mounding it high.
Pour [[0.25 cup]] cold evaporated milk over each glass.
Sprinkle [[1.5 tsp]] sugar over each if you like.
Top with a scoop of ube ice cream.
Serve right away and mix everything together before eating.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C) and boil a kettle of water.
Melt [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat until amber. Pour into a 8-inch round pan or llanera and tilt to coat the bottom.
Whisk the yolks gently with the condensed milk, evaporated milk, lime zest and vanilla without making foam.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into the caramel pan.
Cover the pan tightly with a sheet of foil.
Set the pan in a larger tray and pour hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake for 55 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the center.
Cool, then chill at least 4 hours.
Run a knife around the edge and invert onto a plate.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Soften banana leaves over a flame and line two 8-inch cake pans.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] rice flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, [[0.75 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] coconut milk and [[3 tbsp]] melted butter.
Combine the wet and dry mixtures until smooth.
Pour into the pans and bake for 15 minutes.
Scatter cheese on top and bake 10 minutes more until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Brush with remaining melted butter and finish with coconut.
Serve warm, straight from the pan.
